questions.q: In the currency pair EUR/USD quoted as 1.10, what does the "1.10" represent?
options: 1 US dollar buys 1.10 euros
1 euro buys 1.10 US dollars
The combined value of both currencies in gold
The interest rate differential between the Eurozone and the US
questions.explain: EUR is the base currency and USD is the quote currency, so EUR/USD = 1.10 means 1 euro buys 1.10 US dollars.

questions.q: What is the difference between a spot rate and a forward rate?
options: A spot rate is for near-immediate settlement; a forward rate is agreed today for settlement on a specified future date
A forward rate is always lower than a spot rate
A spot rate only applies to commodities, never currencies
They are two names for exactly the same thing
questions.explain: The spot rate settles almost immediately (typically two business days), while the forward rate is locked in today for an exchange that happens later, just like a forward contract on any other asset.

questions.q: According to covered interest rate parity, if the US interest rate (5%) is higher than the Eurozone interest rate (3%), what should happen to the dollar in the forward market relative to spot?
options: The dollar should trade at a forward premium (stronger forward than spot)
The dollar should trade at a forward discount (weaker forward than spot)
The dollar's forward rate should be completely unrelated to interest rates
The euro's interest rate becomes irrelevant to the forward rate
questions.explain: Covered interest rate parity requires the higher-interest-rate currency to trade at a forward discount, offsetting the interest rate advantage so no risk-free arbitrage exists.

questions.q: Using Forward = Spot × (1 + r_domestic) / (1 + r_foreign) with Spot = 1.10, r_domestic (USD) = 5%, and r_foreign (EUR) = 3%, what is the approximate 1-year forward rate?
options: Approximately 1.0600
Approximately 1.1000 (unchanged from spot)
Approximately 1.1214
Approximately 1.2000

questions.q: Why does a carry trade deliberately avoid using a forward contract to hedge the currency exposure?
options: Forward contracts are illegal for currency trading
Locking in a forward rate would, per covered interest rate parity, erase the interest rate differential the carry trade is trying to capture
Forward contracts can only be used for commodities, not currencies
Using a forward would guarantee a larger profit than staying unhedged
questions.explain: Covered interest rate parity ties the forward rate to the interest rate differential precisely so that hedging removes the profit opportunity. A carry trade stays unhedged, betting that the real-world currency move won't fully offset the rate gap.
